clue.text: They may serve one a wallop, one finishing up in hospital

definitions.text: They may serve one a wallop

indicators.note: in places the finisher inside the name of the hospital, splitting it open

parts.note: Barts is the everyday name of St Bartholomew's, a London teaching hospital
an ender is one who finishes something off

explanation.surface: A warning that someone handing out a wallop may leave a person in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wallop' looks like a punch, but it is British slang for beer. BARTS is St Bartholomew's Hospital in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Bar staff pour drinks, and wallop is old slang for beer, so they serve customers a pint.

clue.text: Duelling Russian character's single shot

parts.note: single means one
a shot is a measure of spirit, such as gin

explanation.surface: A Russian duellist's one bullet fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests a gun in a duel; it is a drink of spirit. The 's in the definition reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushkin's hero Eugene kills his friend Lensky in a duel, making him the duelling Russian of fiction.

clue.text: Have kittens till it's traced

parts.note: to have kittens is to get very anxious, to fret
to till land is to work it

explanation.surface: Someone panicking until something is tracked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'till' looks like 'until'; it is the verb for cultivating soil. 'Have kittens' is a British idiom for being very worried.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental patterns in thin wood are traced and cut out with a saw, so this decoration is something traced.

clue.text: Fruity reviewer right to move south

indicators.note: in a down clue south is lower in the word, so the letter for right shifts further along

parts.note: a critic reviews books, plays or films

explanation.surface: A critic with a fruity voice is told to go south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move south' shifts R two places down the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Citric acid comes from lemons and other citrus fruits, so the adjective describes something of fruit.

clue.text: Soft margarine put in granny's cake

indicators.note: put in places the soft letter and the margarine inside the granny's name

parts.note: nan is a familiar word for a grandmother
P is piano, the musical direction for soft
oleo is short for oleomargarine

explanation.surface: Granny's cake made with soft margarine.
explanation.walkthrough: OLEO, short for oleomargarine, is a crosswordland word for margarine.
explanation.definitionFit: A napoleon is a layered pastry of puff pastry and cream, also called a mille-feuille.

clue.text: Meet to frame a decree

indicators.note: to frame something is to surround it, so the article sits inside

parts.note: meet as an adjective means fit or suitable

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a decree in a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet' is not a verb here; it is the old adjective meaning fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: An authoritative order or command, the Latin 'let it be done'.

clue.text: Drive a ship like Titanic heading off — it will be next to sink

definitions.text: it will be next to sink

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for Drive in an address

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the vessel

parts.note: the Titanic was an ocean liner

explanation.surface: Driving a ship like the Titanic, which is next to sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next to sink' sounds like the Titanic's fate; it means placed beside a kitchen sink.
explanation.definitionFit: A draining board or rack beside the kitchen sink holds washed dishes while they dry.

clue.text: Pensées? French composer has penned fair share

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the share goes inside the composer

parts.note: Léo Delibes wrote the ballet Coppélia
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: A French composer has written his thoughts on getting a fair share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like writing; it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensées is French for thoughts, and careful thoughts or reflections are considered judgments.

clue.text: Type inclined to show stress

parts.note: reads as a person prone to strain, but describes sloping print used for emphasis

explanation.surface: A person who tends to look stressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping print is used to emphasise words, so this typeface leans and stresses.

clue.text: Suffering food poisoning perhaps when a fowl is badly gutted

parts.note: food poisoning makes one ill, sick
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a parrot is a bird, loosely a fowl

explanation.surface: A bird badly gutted gives you food poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like a cleaned bird; it is British slang for bitterly disappointed.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for bitterly disappointed, often heard from footballers after a defeat.

clue.text: Put down creature with fearsome teeth that's bitten one man in suit

indicators.note: having bitten the numeral, the pieces hold it between their jaws

parts.note: lit means landed, as a bird lit on a branch
gator is an informal word for an alligator
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Putting down an alligator that has bitten a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man in suit' suggests clothing; it is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes part in a lawsuit, bringing or contesting a legal case.

clue.text: Teacher's maybe coming through this subject with start of term set back

indicators.note: the opening letter is pushed further back along the word

parts.note: a topic is a subject of discussion

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of term

explanation.surface: A teacher coming through a subject, with term set back.
explanation.walkthrough: Teacher's is a brand of Scotch whisky, not a schoolteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Pub spirits such as a whisky are dispensed through an upturned measure fixed to the bottle.

clue.text: Old leftie welcomes independent African country

indicators.note: welcomes takes the letter in, so it goes inside the name

parts.note: Tony Benn was a veteran left-wing Labour politician

explanation.surface: A veteran socialist welcomes an independent African state.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Benn was a famous left-wing British Labour MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African nation, formerly Dahomey, between Togo and Nigeria.

clue.text: Alternative charts compiled featuring electronic musicians

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

indicators.note: featuring has the letter appear within the rearranged chart letters
compiled means put together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alternative charts compiled featuring electronic musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compiled' shuffles CHARTS, and 'featuring' puts E inside to make CHESTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A large group of instrumental players performing together.

clue.text: In short, County Cricket Club departed abruptly heading for bar

parts.note: abbreviated, County Cricket Club is CCC, a treble C

indicators.note: abruptly cuts off the final letter of the verb

parts.note: departed means left

explanation.surface: A cricket club departing abruptly for the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: CCC, the abbreviation, is three Cs: a treble C. 'abruptly' cuts LEFT to LEF.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol at the start of a musical stave heads the bars that follow it.

clue.text: Stag week to end after heartless bouncer's thrown out

indicators.note: after puts the final letter behind the rearranged letters
thrown out means messed up, so the letters are rearranged
heartless removes the middle letter

parts.note: a bouncer as written; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: to end picks the final letter of week

explanation.surface: A stag week ends after a bouncer throws someone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the N from BOUNCER, 'thrown out' rearranges BOUCER to ROEBUC, and 'to end' takes the K of week.
explanation.definitionFit: The male roe deer is called a buck, so the male is a stag.

clue.text: Everything that is superior in uplifting poetry

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for upper-class or superior

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Superior verse is everything for those who love poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' reverses IN to NI in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos comprises all that exists, everything that has being.

clue.text: Nelson lengthily detained ship of the French

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it
de la means of the in French

explanation.surface: Admiral Nelson held a French ship for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nelson' suggests the admiral; it is the South African leader, jailed for 27 years. 'ship' is a verb meaning to crew.
explanation.definitionFit: The anti-apartheid leader Nelson was imprisoned for twenty-seven years before becoming president.

clue.text: Having some dodgy characters present could make young girl hide

parts.note: a miss is a young girl
a pelt is an animal hide

explanation.surface: Shady characters around might make a girl hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like people; it means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A word with wrong letters in it has some dodgy characters, being spelled wrongly.

clue.text: Irritability of bowels lacking in symptoms at first

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the word in is taken away

parts.note: the intestines are the bowels

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of symptoms

explanation.surface: Irritable bowels with no symptoms at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking in' removes IN from INTESTINES, leaving TESTINES.
explanation.definitionFit: Being touchy and easily annoyed is the quality of being irritable.

clue.text: Go in with American showing guts

parts.note: to go in is to enter

explanation.surface: Going in with an American who shows courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' looks like courage; it is the plural of enteron, the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteron is the zoological word for the alimentary canal, so its plural names intestines.

clue.text: Colourful old singer vacillates somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the word, so the name sits inside it

explanation.surface: A flamboyant veteran singer keeps changing her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colourful' hints at her surname: Cilla Black was a British singer and TV host.
explanation.definitionFit: Cilla Black was a 1960s British pop singer, and her surname is a colour.

clue.text: Stewing like some seafood apparently

definitions.meaning: stewing here means hot, damp and sweaty
read as a word built on a shellfish, it means like a clam

explanation.surface: Something being stewed like seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweaty and damp to the touch, as one is when stewing in heat; and jokingly resembling a bivalve.

clue.text: Chemical making leather without using hydrogen

indicators.note: without using means the element is left out

parts.note: oxhide is leather made from the skin of an ox
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Tanning leather without hydrogen to make a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound of oxygen with another element, such as rust on iron.

clue.text: Press club

definitions.meaning: to press clothes is to smooth them with a hot appliance
a golf club with an angled metal head

explanation.definitionFit: Ironing presses clothes flat, and in golf a numbered metal-headed club is the same word.

clue.text: Entertainer illicitly intercepted reply on telephone

indicators.note: on the telephone words are heard rather than read, so it signals a sound-alike

parts.note: a phone that is illicitly intercepted is tapped, and a reply is an answer

explanation.surface: An entertainer's phone reply secretly intercepted.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'tapped answer' sounds like the performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who performs rhythmic steps in metal-plated shoes is a stage performer.

clue.text: Reflective one among 'Friends' accepting short refusal to be godfather?

indicators.note: reflective suggests a mirror image, so the whole is read backwards
accepting takes the shortened refusal inside the name

parts.note: Ross Geller is one of the six characters in the sitcom Friends

indicators.note: short drops the last letter

parts.note: nope is an informal refusal

explanation.surface: A thoughtful Friends character turns down the role of godfather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts NOPE to NOP, 'accepting' puts it in ROSS, and 'Reflective' reverses ROSNOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: At a christening a godparent stands surety for the child, a role also called sponsor.

clue.text: Making stealthy moves, keen to trap bishop

indicators.note: to trap means to hold within, so the chess letter goes inside

parts.note: to keen is to wail, to lament
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Someone keen to trap a bishop by creeping up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen' looks like eager; it is the verb to wail in grief.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes flames or light flickering softly over a surface, moving lightly and quietly.
